title: Equinor and JAPEX agree asset swap on the Norwegian continental shelf
summary: Equinor and JAPEX have signed two transactions on the Norwegian continental shelf.
body_markdown:
The transactions will simplify the partnership structure in the Norne area and enable optimized value creation in late field life.


The transactions are part of Equinor’s ongoing work to optimise its portfolio on the Norwegian continental shelf and builds on previous agreements with other NCS partners.


Grete Birgitte Haaland, senior vice president for Exploration and Production North in Equinor


Photo: Andreas Kleiberg / ©Equinor


"These transactions are in line with our strategy on the Norwegian shelf to increase value creation and develop our resources faster. The agreements strengthen our position in the Norne area while allowing us to retain a substantial interest in Goliat”, says Grete Birgitte Haaland, senior vice president for Exploration and Production North in Equinor.


Under the agreements, Equinor will transfer an 8% interest in the Goliat field to JAPEX, while retaining a 27% non-operated interest. Equinor will also transfer a 20% interest in the exploration acreages Arkenstone and a 10% interest in Rhadamanthys. Both located in the Norwegian Sea.


As part of the transactions, JAPEX will carry a portion of Equinor’s costs for the planned exploration wells in both licence areas up to an agreed maximum amount.


In return, Equinor will acquire JAPEX’s 3.5% participating interest in the Verdande field. The acquisition will increase Equinor’s ownership in Verdande from approximately 59.3% to approximately 62.8%.


The transactions will be implemented through two linked agreements. The divestments in Goliat, Arkenstone and Rhadamanthys will have an effective date of 1 January 2026, while the acquisition of the Verdande interest will have an effective date of 1 January 2027.


Completion of the transactions remains subject to customary conditions, including relevant regulatory approvals.
